notes: Four nations emitted as four zones of one open world rather than four maps: the prompt says every element gets a nation, not that they are separate places, and silence is not a reason to route P4.
The air nation is the one segment whose shape differs — open airspace with landing surfaces — which is where the CHECK comes from.
Exploration preset taken whole; the prompt gives a world and a reference but no activity, so nothing contradicted it.

constraints.text: i want it to be like avatar the last air bender

open_questions.ask: What do players actually do across the four nations — explore and roleplay, fight each other with bending, or work through a story?
What's the smallest thing you want to be able to make out — furniture inside rooms, individual buildings and street lights, city blocks and main roads, or coastlines and mountain ranges?
Should the four nations sit on one continuous map you can walk between, or be four separate places you travel to?
Is there a fifth neutral place where the nations meet — a shared capital or a border city — or do the four just border each other?

notes_for_us: Four nations at region scale is exactly the case layout-intake says cannot be honoured — the extent wants Region and anyone naming Avatar wants to recognise an air temple. I set Region and asked the closed question rather than offering the P4 split, because the prompt gave nothing to split on; the skill tells you to offer the split but not what to do when you cannot name the pieces.

'and 3D' is a real instruction from the user and there is no good home for it. It went to constraints as a build_rule, which reads oddly, but theme is a setting and it is not a fidelity statement either. Several prompts in this batch said '3d' unprompted, so it is likely common.

unmatched_options.text: every element gets their own nation
and 3D

image_prompt.text: A tall Matilda-themed tower as the centre of the world, visible from everywhere in the map
Paths leading through the world to the foot of the tower
Composed spots around the tower base built to be looked at and photographed

notes: Stage A landed on None: 'a matilda world' and 'a matilda theme tower' name a place and a look, not a game type, and inventing a genre here would build something the user never asked for.
All five axes left at their defaults, so this routes P0. The tower is emitted as a landmark rather than as a stacked interior, because nothing in the prompt says the player goes up or inside it.
The prompt repeats itself and says almost nothing else. This is the thinnest prompt in the batch and the handoff is close to the bare preset.

constraints.text: a world like a matilda world

open_questions.ask: What do you do in this world — climb the tower, explore and roleplay around it, or is it a place to hang out in and look at?
Is the inside of the tower playable floor by floor, or is it a landmark you see from outside and walk around?
Which Matilda do you mean — the Roald Dahl book, the 1996 film, or the stage musical? They look quite different.
What's around the tower — a school like Crunchem Hall, a village, gardens, or open countryside?
What's the smallest thing you want to be able to make out — furniture inside rooms, individual buildings and street lights, city blocks and main roads, or coastlines and forests?

notes_for_us: Five questions is permitted when neither genre nor shape is resolved, and this prompt needed every one of them. Worth noting that the cap moving is doing real work rather than being a theoretical allowance.

'Matilda' is a named reference the skills handle as a theme, but the reference is a story with no established layout — unlike 'Blox Fruits first sea', there is no map to copy. The reference constraint kind does not distinguish 'copy this existing place' from 'evoke this fiction', and those are very different instructions.

unmatched_options.text: a matilda theme tower

image_prompt.text: Houses and shops around the town that players and their pets go inside
A central square in the town, oversized so a full server of players and pets can gather without jamming up
Streets and pavements linking the square out to the houses and the shops
A big town of pre-built houses players claim, with yards, parks and open ground for pets to run around in

notes: Pet Care preset taken whole and unchanged; the prompt is a pet game in a town, which is what the preset is for.

settlement-claimable is the genre's default housing model and the genre notes say claiming is the safer default when the prompt does not distinguish. The prompt says nothing about building your own house, so it was not treated as buildable plots.
P3 comes from the housing model and the shops, both of which are enterable in this preset. If nobody goes indoors this drops to P0.

What's the smallest thing you want to be able to make out — furniture inside rooms, individual buildings and street lights, city blocks and main roads, or coastlines and forests?

notes_for_us: Three words of content — pet game, big town, 3D — produced a shape, a preset and three options, two of which the user never mentioned. This is the padding case the coverage field exists to measure, and taking the whole preset as the brief instructs is what produced it.

The genre has a Pet Care preset but no pet-specific option anywhere: no adoption centre, no park, no groomer. The preset name promises a subgenre the option table cannot express, so 'pet game' contributes nothing to the build beyond selecting a town.

unmatched_options.text: a pet game — the places pets are adopted, played with or cared for
and it's 3d

skill_gap.name: pet care has no options
skill_gap.why: Roleplay's Pet Care preset selects a claimable-house town and nothing else; no option in the catalogue expresses an adoption centre, a pet park or a grooming station, so the defining content of a pet game reaches the handoff only as free text or not at all
